notes:
HEADCOUNTS: most site figures are the "annual average employees" each establishment reported to OSHA on Form 300A, read from OSHA's published establishment files (2025 file, submissions through 31 August 2026; 2024 file where the 2025 one has no row). They are the employer's own count for that street address, exclude contractors, and are cited by the file URL; the establishment name as filed is given in each employeesNote. Where a company page or economic-development source gives a different figure it is quoted in the note. Bell: "Textron" is deliberately not listed as an alias of Bell (Textron has other subsidiaries: Textron Aviation service centres, Kautex, Textron Systems); existing "Textron" rows around Fort Worth and Amarillo are very likely Bell sites and should be reviewed by hand. Bell has not yet filed for 2025, so its figures are 2024. Smaller Bell buildings left out: Plant 2 Hurst (323), Commercial Business Center (331), Plant 6 Arlington flight research (223), Plant 3 (139), Manufacturing Technology Center (96). General Motors: GM says it employs over 9,000 in Texas, but that includes GM Financial and the Austin technical centre, so no state manufacturing figure is given. Tarrant County's list shows 10,512 for the Arlington plant, which matches nothing GM reports and was not used. Tesla: the Megapack factory near Brookshire and the lithium refinery near Robstown belong to other industries and are left to other briefs. SpaceX: McGregor is a test site rather than a factory but is one of the company's three large Texas sites; the Bastrop Starlink plant is filed under Computer and Electronic Product Manufacturing, as SpaceX reports it. Boeing is the one large plant that could not be placed (see unplaced); its site is real and current. Boeing was not written as a company entry because a company with no plant would load nothing. Safran: three separate Safran businesses are grouped under one company entry because the database is likely to hold them under Safran or their former names (Zodiac, Weber Aircraft, Labinal, Turbomeca). No headcount was found for the Grand Prairie engine site. Red Oak: Bombardier and Qarbon Aerospace occupy the two halves of the former Triumph (Vought) aerostructures campus on Austin Blvd; existing "Triumph Aerostructures" rows there belong to one or the other and were not listed as an alias of either. Schaeffler: the Seguin plant still files as Vitesco Technologies USA LLC; "Continental" is not listed as an alias because Continental still operates other Texas sites under its own name. Airbus Helicopters: final assembly is in Mississippi; Grand Prairie is the headquarters, completion and repair site. It is kept because it is on every state and regional list of aerospace plants; no site headcount could be read on an open page (about 500 to 600 is commonly reported). Trinity Industries: only the Longview tank car plant is listed. Its Saginaw sites (about 280 people each in the OSHA file) are railcar maintenance shops, and Plant 200 in Longview closed in 2025. Seatrium AmFELS (Brownsville shipyard) is left out: the yard was sold to Karpowership in January 2026 after its last projects were delivered, and its 2025 OSHA average had fallen to 180. Gulf Copper's Galveston and Port Arthur yards (now Davie Defense, about 180 each) and Sterling Shipyard in Port Neches (265) are below the size cut and were not researched further. Left out on purpose: Blue Origin at Van Horn (587, a launch and engine test site), Gulfstream Dallas (561, a completion and service centre), StandardAero and Dallas Airmotive (engine overhaul), Vutex (1,034, parts sequencing at Toyota), Avancez in Arlington (909, module assembly for GM), Toyotetsu Texas (540, inside the Toyota campus), Recaro Aircraft Seating in Fort Worth (484), Dynacraft in McKinney (464, a PACCAR parts plant), US Farathane in Austin (568, plastics, another brief's industry). Applied Materials (Austin, NAICS 333242) is semiconductor machinery and so falls in Machinery Manufacturing; an electronics brief may also carry it under the same name. Oilfield equipment: Baker Hughes, SLB, Halliburton, NOV and TechnipFMC run many mid-sized Texas plants rather than one large one. Only plants that file with OSHA under machinery manufacturing (or, for TechnipFMC Houston, a campus known for it) and could be placed are listed; what each makes is taken from the establishment's filed name and industry code, and where those say nothing specific the products line says only "Oil and gas field equipment".
